correctness.rationale: Full proof reconstructs and inverts the exact m-by-m Gram matrix, with r_i>0, Z>r_i and strict kernel vertex signs. The kernel positive region is exactly a simplex cap: scale ratios and average establish H_i. Reproduction of constants yields 2H_i-1, convexity gives vertex maximum, and opposite-sign kernels on sets of positive uniform volume give strict nonvertex inequality. The single-atom kernel formula, strict derivative, Taylor coefficient and limit are checked symbolically and by independent exact-rational checker in 24 weighted cases and 13 one-atom dimensions. Finite checks are supplementary, not universal proof.

originality.rationale: A complete arbitrary-nonnegative-vertex-weight endpoint formula is proved for a mixed uniform-volume plus discrete vertex-atomic simplex measure, including strict vertex localization and positivity extremizers. The volume-only exact simplex case, an absolutely continuous Dirichlet-weight case, and metric-star vertex atom models do not imply the mixed-measure formula or its strict second-order single-atom instability. Full original texts inspected for the two closest accessible foundational papers. Priority in unindexed mass-lumping literature remains a candid risk; source comparison supports originality to best available evidence, not uniqueness.
residual_risks: Unindexed mass-lumping or least-squares numerical-analysis literature may contain an equivalent all-weight formula.
The 2001 mass-lumping paper was available as an abstract only; no full-text noncoverage claim is made about it.
Independently published full-text comparison beyond the inspected primary works is still warranted before external priority attribution.

value.rationale: The complete natural m-parameter weighted simplex problem has an exact sharp L-infinity projector norm, positivity defect and all maximizing evaluations, rather than a generic bound. In the one-atom family it exhibits counterintuitive nonlocal norm growth, precisely identified unweighted norming vertices, and zero linear but positive quadratic perturbation. This is an interpretable endpoint stability invariant for mixtures of continuous local least squares and vertex quadrature, useful across simplex dimensions; not an arbitrary isolated example.
